# 5-Day Lisbon Itinerary for History, Food, and Viewpoints

A moderate-pace plan for 2 adults, built around Lisbon’s historic neighborhoods, scenic overlooks, and local food stops. Costs below are estimated per person in CAD and stay within your **CAD 900** sightseeing budget, excluding flights and hotel.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Plan

Day 1: Alfama, Baixa, and riverside first look
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and take a gentle walk through **Baixa** to Commerce Square and the riverfront.
- Afternoon: Explore **Alfama** on foot, including Lisbon Cathedral and a slow wander through narrow lanes.
- Food: Try a simple first meal of **bacalhau** or grilled sardines in a traditional tasca.
- Transit: Airport metro or taxi to central Lisbon; then walk and use tram/metro as needed.
- Rainy-day backup: Visit the **Lisbon Story Centre** or the **MUDE design museum**.

Estimated cost per person: **CAD 95-120**

Day 2: Belém landmarks and pastries
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Belém Tower** and the **Monument to the Discoveries** for the best light and fewer crowds.
- Afternoon: Visit the **Jerónimos Monastery** and the **National Coach Museum** if you want more history.
- Food: Stop for **pastéis de nata** at a classic Belém bakery and keep lunch casual nearby.
- Transit: Tram 15 or a rideshare from central Lisbon; Belém is easy for a half-day cluster.
- Rainy-day backup: Spend extra time at the **Coach Museum** and the **MAAT**.

Estimated cost per person: **CAD 110-140**

Day 3: Bairro Alto, Chiado, and scenic viewpoints
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Start in **Chiado** with a coffee stop and a relaxed walk through bookshops and historic streets.
- Afternoon: Visit **Santa Justa Lift** area, then walk to **Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara** for a classic city view.
- Food: Have lunch at a small seafood or petiscos spot; save room for a late-afternoon pastry or gelato.
- Transit: Mostly walk; use the metro for longer hops and avoid unnecessary backtracking.
- Rainy-day backup: Browse **Livraria Bertrand** and nearby cafés, then add a museum stop such as the **National Museum of Contemporary Art**.

Estimated cost per person: **CAD 80-110**

Day 4: Castelo, Graça, and tram-side viewpoints
- Morning: Visit **São Jorge Castle** for history and one of the best panoramic views in the city.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Graça** and the nearby miradouros for a slower scenic walk.
- Food: Choose a neighborhood lunch with soup, grilled fish, or bifana sandwiches.
- Transit: Use tram, bus, or a short taxi ride for the uphill sections; walking works well downhill.
- Rainy-day backup: Replace the castle visit with the **National Tile Museum** and a long café stop.

Estimated cost per person: **CAD 100-130**

Day 5: Market, final viewpoints, and departure buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- Morning: Visit **Time Out Market** or a local market for a flexible brunch and last food tasting.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/aa/Delivery_point_inside_the_Time_Out_Market_Lisbon%2C_Portugal_%2855121417511%29.jpg Alt=Morning: Visit **Time Out Market** or a local market for a flexible brunch and last food tasting, Lisbon, Portugal. Build A Day-
- Afternoon: Pick one final viewpoint, such as **Miradouro da Senhora do Monte**, then shop for small souvenirs.
- Food: Keep it light with seafood, pastries, or a final tasting menu if you want a nicer farewell meal.
- Transit: Stay central, then use metro or taxi to the airport depending on your flight time.
- Rainy-day backup: Spend the afternoon in the **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** or a covered shopping arcade.

Estimated cost per person: **CAD 90-125**

## Budget Fit and Transit Strategy

| Item | Estimated per person | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Day 1 | CAD 95-120 | Light sightseeing, easy arrival day |
| Day 2 | CAD 110-140 | Belém entry fees and pastry stop |
| Day 3 | CAD 80-110 | Mostly walking, low-cost day |
| Day 4 | CAD 100-130 | Castle and viewpoint day |
| Day 5 | CAD 90-125 | Flexible final day |
| Total | CAD 475-625 | Leaves room for upgraded meals, taxis, or extra admissions |

- **Best transit mix:** walk in the historic core, use the **metro** for longer links, and take **tram 15** to Belém.
- **Taxi/rideshare use:** good for airport transfers, uphill sections, or late evenings.
- **Budget control:** keep one paid museum or monument per day, and use viewpoints and neighborhood walks as your low-cost anchors.
